html:
Mohamed Nasheed is a Maldivian politician who became the country's first democratically elected president in 2008, after years as a jailed dissident. He was born in Male in 1967.

He beat Maumoon Abdul Gayoom in the first multiparty election. In 2009 he held a cabinet meeting underwater, in scuba gear, to show the world that rising seas threaten the islands, and he became a leading voice for small states at climate talks such as the 2009 Copenhagen summit.

In 2012 he resigned under pressure from police and soldiers, in what he called a coup. He was later jailed on terrorism charges widely seen as political, went into exile, and returned to serve as speaker of parliament. His rise and fall mark the uneven path of democracy in the Maldives.
